draft.title: Hooke's law
card: For an ideal spring, the extension x is directly proportional to the force applied. Doubling the force doubles the extension.
Hooke's law is F = -kx. The spring constant k is the force needed per metre of extension, in N/m. A stiffer spring has a larger k.
The minus sign shows that the spring's restoring force points opposite to the extension. The size of the force is kx.
A stretched or compressed spring stores elastic potential energy. E = ½kx², so doubling the extension makes the stored energy four times greater.
draft.remember: Force is proportional to extension, F = kx in size. Stored energy is ½kx².

a.q: A spring stretches 0.10 m when a 5.0 N force is applied. What is its spring constant k, assuming it is ideal?
a.why: k = F ÷ x = 5.0 ÷ 0.10 = 50 N/m. Multiplying force by extension gives 0.50, which is not the force per metre.
a.clue: Divide the force by the extension in metres.

b.q: Spring A is stretched 2.0 cm and stores energy E. Spring A is then stretched 6.0 cm from rest. How much energy does it store now?
b.why: Stored energy is ½kx², so it depends on the square of the extension. Tripling x makes the energy 3² = 9 times greater. Choosing 3E treats energy as proportional to extension, which is true for force but not for energy.
b.clue: Energy depends on x squared, not x.
